recipes.name: Easy Creole Okra and Shrimp
ingredients_raw: 3 cooked andouille sausage, cut into quarters
1 (10 ounce) package frozen cut okra, thawed
2 tablespoons Cajun seasoning, or to taste
2 pounds peeled and deveined medium shrimp (30-40 per pound)

steps.text: Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Stir in the bell pepper and onion; cook and stir until the onion has softened and turned translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in the tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes, then add the okra, sausage, Cajun seasoning, and salt. Cover and cook for 30 minutes. Stir in the shrimp and cook until they are bright pink on the outside and the meat is no longer transparent in the center, 8 to 12 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Creole Okra and Shrimp
raw_recipe.description: Shrimp is simmered in a spicy tomato sauce with okra and andouille sausage.

review.reviewBody: Many Cajun "stews" also use chopped celery and minced garlic, which I added to this. Because I like Cajun food a bit on the spicy side, I used RoTel tomatoes rather than regular ones, also, and I used fresh okra (which I cut up myself) as well (but frozen okra will do just fine, as long as its unbreaded). A word of caution: Cajun/Creole pre-mixed spice, such as Tony Chachere's or Zatarain's, already has plenty of salt in it, as well as red pepper and other spices. If you use the spice, don't use additional salt. Instead, just use the Cajun/Creole spice to taste, and if you want a bit more zip, you can splash a dash or two of Tabasco onto your serving, which won't substantially add salt. Serve it up with some hot garlic bread, and you've got a quick, simple meal in itself. Also, if you want a twist, rather than adding shrimp, boil a couple or three chicken breasts until they're cooked, cut them into chunks, and make chicken and andouille stew. You'll love it!

This turned out phenomenal! Tasted just like I remember as a kid. This was actually my favorite of all the things my mom cooked for dinner. I did not add any meat as I'll add a meat serving to the serving I eat in order to have flexibility . My only alterations were adding celery with the bell peppers and onion as suggested by other raters and instead of 2 cans of dIced tomatoes I used one with 2 cans of 8oz tomatoes sauce. I also did not have time for okra to thaw but it still came out great. Will definitely be making this again and again.

I've made this recipe several times. I use salted butter to saute my veggies, and I add celery to it. Sometimes I add chicken, but I cook it first. I will also add a can of rotel, depending on who I'm cooking for. It is always a hit with my coworkers!!

I rated this based on the original recipe not the version I made with other ingredients. The only thing I added were two cans of regular Rotel but won't do that when I make it again. I may add one, but not two. I also will use 3 cans of diced tomatoes. Two cans just weren't enough. I will also skip the salt or just use half. It was way too salty for me. I also used fresh okra but will try frozen next time. Fresh okra lengthened the cooking time quite a bit.
We love this! Changes we made, used 2 Rotel with green chilies and 1 Rotel with habanero (10 Oz cans). So no cajun seasoning needed. Also added scallops and garlic. Nice heat and flavor!
I added 2 tsp. Of Tony Chachaere’s creole spice and that was spicy enough.

Delicious! I was born and raised in Louisiana so I’m used to food like this with spice. I made the recipe as printed and used Tony’s Chachere’s and got the spice I wanted and salt to get the saltiness I wanted also some garlic and onion powder. I season to taste. I cooked rice also for it. I bought medium shrimp already cooked and only had to take the tail off. I just stirred it into the hot dish. I did not cook the shrimp in it. Whoever said it was bland made it wrong. Also some like bland but we love spicy. I season to taste so I don’t always measure unless I’m baking. My husband said it’s the best I’ve ever made. Just tweak it.

I did make some changes, just to use what I had, but nothing too major (28 oz crushed tomatoes + 14.5 diced) so I can still speak to the original recipe. Added celery and garlic because my grandmother always made it that way. I accidentally used creole seasoning (Tony Chachere’s) and 2T was too much (salty) but it was still very very good. My husband wants me to make it again tonight 😂
I have made this recipe several times. I use 2 cans of Rotel and no salt. The Cajun seasoning has plenty of salt for me. Very tasty and very easy to make.
Yes I will salute my onions bell peppers by their self and then saute okra by itself and add the stew tomatoes in last and cook rice by it self

I didn't use any oil because the fat from the sausage is enough. I used beef sausage, but deer sausage would be even better. Also, I added garlic. It turned out great and doesn't take long at all to cook.
I doubled the amount, because I was cooking for a larger group. It still came out very well.

Tasty and easy to make. Always a hit at our family bbq. Some people don’t enjoy the hot spicy flavour as much, so make sure to adjust for your crowd. You can always provide spices separately for those who like more of a bite.
My family and I love this recipe and use it often. Reminds me of the shrimp and okra my dad used to make when I was a kid.
I made this, substituting rotisserie chicken and bacon for the shrimp and sausage. I added celery and a can of Rotel tomatoes. Served with rice, it was great!!
Absolutely delicious! My family and I enjoyed every morsel! Great recipe! A keeper!
This is THE BEST. Very flavorful my hubby loves this recipe.
A little under sauced. I ended up using an additional can of diced tomatoes.
I slow cooked it, that's all.
I added one can of crushed tomatoes.
